messages:
Incident Bot: ALERT: Increased 5xx rate on /v1/generate from 17:02 UTC, service=runtime-tokenizer, noise=spike, paging oncall Maya (oncall). Automated mitigation suggestions: scale replicas, throttle ingestion.
Maya (oncall): i'm on it. seeing 5xx from a subset of tokenizer pods. paging team.
Nina R: what's the error? OOM? CUDA?
Maya (oncall): early logs show kernel OOM on node ip-10-2-45-3, containers getting SIGKILL. not GPU errors. looks like user prompt decoding causing CPU path blowup.
Chris L: can you paste the pod describe + OOM messages?
Maya (oncall): pasting snippets:
```
/var/log/messages: kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 21432 (tokenizer) score 754 or sacrifice child
kubectl logs tokenizer-5f6d7 -c tokenizer | tail -n 50
ERROR: tokenizer: prefix_decode() exceeded budget, allocating huge map
OOMKilled
```
Maya (oncall): kubectl top nodes shows cpu spiking to 98% on that node. other nodes fine.
Deploy Bot: deploy pipeline: recent change 1799400000 -> tokenizer: increase max_decode_threads=8 deployed 2 hours ago.
Chris L: that config change would increase CPU per request. roll back asap.
Maya (oncall): mitigation plan initial: 1) roll back max_decode_threads change; 2) cordon node with repeated evictions; 3) scale tokenizer replicas down to reduce concurrent decoding; 4) apply a temporary rate-limit on /v1/generate for experimental orgs.
Nina R: agree. rollback first.
Maya (oncall): rolling back now -> `kubectl set image deployment/tokenizer tokenizer=tokenizer:v1.14.2 --record`
Maya (oncall): started. also pushing a quick initcontainer patch to set ulimits and cgroups for CPU to avoid single-process domination.
Priya (CS): Priya (CS) here — which customers impacted? i'm seeing alerts from org-842 and org-99 complaining about timeouts.
Maya (oncall): affected: org-842 (partner embedder), org-99 (internal test), several anonymous API keys reporting 503/504s. severity: degraded but not data-loss.
Chris L: temporary routing option: route traffic for org-842 to dedicated lighter model (gpt-compat-lt) until stable.
Maya (oncall): applying rate limit to org-842 now: `redwoodctl traffic update --org 842 --qps 2 --route gpt-compat-lt`
Maya (oncall): applied. their error rate dropped ~55%.
Sam M: taking over oncall in 10. handing off notes: rolled back decode_threads, cordoned node ip-10-2-45-3, scaled tokenizer down from 20->12, rate-limited org-842 and org-99, created follow-up ticket INF-2193 to add safeties (per-request cpu limiter, default decode_threads=4).
Maya (oncall): adding logs/diagnostics collected: heap profiles + pprof link https://ci.internal/pprof/1799501234
Maya (oncall): root cause hypothesis: config change increased parallel decoding per request; a small subset of prompts trigger pathological combinatorial decode leading to huge memory map allocations on CPU path -> OOM -> OOM killer -> pod kill.
Chris L: longer term: add input length/complexity estimator that rejects or queues problematic prompts, knob to fallback to streaming decode with lower memory footprint.
Priya (CS): i've informed customers and offered temporary credits. will keep them updated.
Incident Bot: Incident assigned -> incident/2026-03-15-1799501234, severity=P2, runbook=tokenizer-cpu-oom. Channels: #incidents, pagerduty.
Sam M: accepted. I'll monitor for next 2 hours and run a canary with decode_threads=4.
Maya (oncall): thanks team. leaving notes in incident doc and creating postmortem draft.
Maya (oncall): final status at handoff: traffic restored to 90% baseline, no new pod evictions in 18m. handing off to Sam.
Sam M: acknowledged. :thumbsup:
